prompt: Capture a quick idea in my vault: quantum computing for ML acceleration, tag it as an idea.
context: Vault at /Users/me/Vault (contains .obsidian/). Obsidian app is running.
rubric: Resolves the vault path (ancestor folder containing .obsidian, or asks the user) before writing
Uses the Obsidian CLI `obsidian create name=... content=...` because the app is running
Sets the tags property with `obsidian property:set name=tags value="[idea,quantum]" type=list`
Writes YAML frontmatter with the expected default properties (tags/aliases/created)
Notes the file-based alternative when the app is not running
anti_patterns: Writes a file to an arbitrary path without resolving the vault
Puts tags in the body as #tags when the user asked for a tagged note and properties are the vault convention
gold_notes: CLI when the app is live; file-based for CI/CD and bulk edits. Property types: text, list, number, checkbox, date, datetime.

prompt: Find everything in my vault about Project X.
context: Vault at /Users/me/Vault, ~340 notes. Semantic index already built.
rubric: Runs a text search: `obsidian search query="Project X"` or `obsidian search:context`
Runs the semantic search script for conceptual matches: `python scripts/semantic_search.py --vault . --action ask --query ...`
Uses at least one Obsidian search operator correctly (tag:, path:, file:, content:, [property:value])
Explains the difference between literal and semantic hits in the results
anti_patterns: Uses grep over the vault as the only method
Invents a search operator that is not in the reference table
gold_notes: Operators: file:, path:, tag:, content:, line:, section:, task:, task-todo:, [property:value].

prompt: Every note tagged #draft should get status: review.
rubric: Uses the bulk script rather than per-note CLI calls: `python scripts/bulk_properties.py --vault . --filter "tag:#draft" --set "status=review"`
States that the operation edits many files and suggests a dry run or a git/vault backup first
Uses the correct property type when the value is not plain text (--type list/checkbox)
Reports how many notes were changed
anti_patterns: Applies a bulk frontmatter rewrite with no backup or confirmation

prompt: Audit my vault's links — I think a lot of them are broken.
rubric: Runs `python scripts/link_audit.py --vault /Users/me/Vault` for the full report
Also mentions the targeted CLI commands: `obsidian unresolved`, `obsidian orphans`, `obsidian deadends`
Reports the metric set: total links, resolved %, unresolved, orphans, dead-ends
Distinguishes unresolved links from orphan notes and dead-end notes
Proposes fixing with `vault_cleanup.py --action report` before `--action fix`
anti_patterns: Runs the cleanup in fix mode before showing the report
Conflates orphans (no incoming links) with dead-ends (no outgoing links)

prompt: Clean up my vault: empty notes, duplicates, orphan attachments.
context: Vault at /Users/me/Vault, not under version control.
rubric: Runs `python scripts/vault_health.py --vault .` first to see the state
Runs `vault_cleanup.py --action report` as a dry run before any change
Only then runs `--action fix`, after the user has seen the report
Warns that the vault is not version-controlled and recommends a backup first
Lists what cleanup touches: empty notes, broken links, duplicates, frontmatter, orphan attachments, tag casing, stale TODOs
anti_patterns: Deletes attachments without reporting them first
gold_notes: Destructive vault operations always go report -> review -> fix.

prompt: Reorganize my vault with the PARA method.
context: Vault at /Users/me/Vault, flat structure, notes tagged project/area/resource/archive.
rubric: Scaffolds the structure: `python scripts/scaffold_vault.py --vault . --template para`
Moves notes with `organize_vault.py --strategy by-tag` and an explicit tag-to-folder mapping
Warns that moving notes can break links and recommends a link audit afterwards
Mentions the other available templates (zettelkasten, gtd, journal, research, custom)
anti_patterns: Moves files with shell mv and leaves links unchecked
Invents a template name that the script does not support
